## SuperSubtitler 0.3.2 — speaker changes: more quick replies, much faster

Download both files into one folder: `SuperSubtitlerGUI.exe` (the window) and `SuperSubtitler.exe` (the engine).

### 🗨️ “Mark speaker changes” works differently now
- Testing showed the weak spot: two people speaking quickly one after the other often went unnoticed — one subtitle, two speakers, no “- ” lines.
- The reason: until now the voices were told apart across the whole film. That needs plenty of speech per person, so a one-second reply was simply counted to whoever spoke before.
- Subtitles never show *who* speaks, only *where the voice changes*. So that is all SuperSubtitler looks for now: the pyannote segmentation model, trained exactly for this, judges every second about nine times, and a change counts where enough of those looks agree.
- Measured on hand-labelled recordings (66 minutes of debates and news, 1–11 speakers):

| | changes found | quick replies found | found changes that are real |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3.1 | 67 % | 46 % | 73 % |
| **0.3.2** | **73 %** | **58 %** | **73 %** |

- **About 8 times faster:** a 2-hour film needs roughly 2 minutes instead of 10–15.
- **Smaller:** only a 6 MB model; sherpa-onnx and the speaker embedding are no longer needed.
- New setting *How sure a speaker change must be* (`speaker_change_threshold`, 0.15 measured best). The old speaker settings of 0.3.0/0.3.1 are replaced automatically.
- Honest limit: quick replies are the hardest case for every system; about 4 in 10 of them still go unnoticed.

The exes are not code-signed; Windows SmartScreen may warn — "More info" → "Run anyway". Built by GitHub Actions.
